newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Peregrine Vietnam boss held in tax probe.
newsitem.headline: Peregrine Vietnam boss held in tax probe.

text.p: State investigators in southern Vietnam's Ho Chi Minh City said on Tuesday they had arrested the head of Hong Kong-based Peregrine Capital Vietnam Limited on tax evasion charges.
They said Nguyen Trung Truc, an Australian-Vietnamese businessman, was arrested on Monday, but gave no other details.

Alan Mercer, chief legal counsel with Peregrine Investment Holdings in Hong Kong, said the firm had not been given details of the charges but said Australian embassy officials were seeking Truc's release on bail.
"Mr Truc is an Australian national, obviously an employee of the Peregrine group. We are concerned about his well being," Mercer said by telephone from Hong Kong.
"He has been arrested in relation to certain tax offences. We believe they relate to personal tax affairs," he added.
Vietnam announced fines and punitive steps against Peregrine Capital Vietnam in March following a lengthy investigation into alleged business irregularities.
But a separate probe into the tax affairs of Truc and his family members has continued.
Truc, one of the most prominent foreign businessmen in Vietnam, has had his passport withheld since the investigation began in May last year.
His wife was also prevented from leaving Vietnam, but officials said the arrest warrant named only Truc.

A Ho Chi Minh City official, who declined to be identified, said Truc's case was likely to come to court within four months of the date of arrest. Details of the possible fines or penalties against Truc were not available.
